title: 230 V copper TPS (2C+E) – guidance
source: Prysmian Cable Guide (Australia), 2-core PVC 75 °C, 40 °C ambient; Olex handbook gives the same mV/A·m
note: Guidance only, not a substitute for AS/NZS 3008.1.1. Ratings are for one circuit at 40 °C ambient; grouping with other circuits reduces them further. AS/NZS 3000 allows 5% total drop from the point of supply (11.5 V at 230 V), including mains and submains. 16 mm² buried values look high in the source table – treat with caution.
methods: Air all round the cable – best cooling.
Clipped to a wall or batten; the surface blocks some cooling.
Air trapped in the conduit insulates the cable – roughly 10–15% lower.
Solar heating adds to conductor temperature.
One side against ceiling batts – heat can only escape one way.
Buried in batts – about half the free-air rating. Avoid, or upsize.
Air gap in the conduit lowers it slightly vs buried direct.
